cohort: 955 nulliparous women with nonanomalous, singleton, vertex, term pregnancies undergoing labor induction with intact membranes at a tertiary-care academic hospital from January 2015 to April 2017
finding: While the chance of vaginal delivery decreased after 24 hours of labor induction, it remained nearly 50% even beyond 60 hours, and the risks of hemorrhage and maternal infection, though increasing modestly over time, were primarily observed in women who underwent cesarean delivery.
